'''Tadashi Tokieda''' (Japanese: 時枝正; born 1968) is a Japanese [[mathematician]], working in [[mathematics]] and [[physics]]. He is a professor of mathematics at [[Stanford University]]; he formerly was a fellow and Director of Studies of Mathematics at [[Trinity Hall, Cambridge|Trinity Hall]], [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge]]. He also invents, collects, and studies toys that uniquely reveal and explore real-world surprises of mathematics and physics. In comparison with most mathematicians, he had an unusual path in life: he started as a painter, and then became a classical [[Philology|philologist]], before transitioning to mathematics. Tokieda is known for his public lectures where he demonstrates mathematical phenomena. 

==Life and career==
Tokieda was born in [[Tokyo]] and initially intended to be a painter.<ref>{{Cite interview |last=Tokieda |first=Tadashi |interviewer=Brady Haran |title=An Educated Adult |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qrJCm10ajJw |access-date=July 11, 2022 |work=Numberphile |place=California |date=July 11, 2022}}</ref> He then studied at [[Lycée Sainte-Marie Grand Lebrun]]<ref name="数学まなびはじめ 第3集" /> in [[France]] as a classical [[philology|philologist]]. According to his personal homepage, he taught himself basic mathematics from Russian collections of problems.

He is a 1989 classics graduate from [[Sophia University]]<ref name="数学まなびはじめ 第3集" /> in Tokyo and has a 1991 bachelor's degree from [[University of Oxford|Oxford]] in mathematics (where he studied as a British Council Fellow). He obtained his PhD at [[Princeton University|Princeton]] in 1996 under the supervision of [[William Browder (mathematician)|William Browder]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tadashi Tokieda - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=60734 |website=[[University of North Dakota]]}}</ref>

Tokieda joined the University of Illinois at Urbana Champaign as a J. L. Doob Research Assistant Professor for the 1997 academic year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Math Times - Fall 1997 |url=https://math.illinois.edu/system/files/inline-files/MathTimesFA97.pdf |website=[[Illinois.edu]]}}</ref>

He has been involved in the [[African Institute for Mathematical Sciences]] since its founding in 2003.

In 2004, he was elected a Fellow of Trinity Hall, where he became the Director of Studies in Mathematics and the Stephan and Thomas Körner Fellow.<ref>{{Cite web |title=homepage |url=https://www.trinhall.cam.ac.uk/contact/contact-directory-profile.asp?ItemID=1938 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160605014114/https://www.trinhall.cam.ac.uk/contact/contact-directory-profile.asp?ItemID=1938 |archive-date=2016-06-05 |website=[[Trinity Hall, Cambridge]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Tadashi Tokieda's bio |url=https://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/~tokieda/Tokieda_bio.html |website=[[Cam.ac.uk]] |access-date=2016-05-08 |archive-date=2016-06-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160605000931/https://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/~tokieda/Tokieda_bio.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He was the William and Flora Hewlett Foundation Fellow in 2013–2014 at the [[Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study]] at [[Harvard University]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=25 September 2013 |title=Tadashi Tokieda |url=https://www.radcliffe.harvard.edu/people/tadashi-tokieda |website=Harvard.edu}}</ref>

In the 2015–2016 academic year he was the Poincaré Distinguished Visiting Professor at Stanford.<ref>{{Cite web |title=homepage |url=http://mathematics.stanford.edu/people/department-directory/name/tadashi-tokieda/ |website=[[Stanford.edu]] |access-date=2016-05-08 |archive-date=2016-04-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422172102/http://mathematics.stanford.edu/people/department-directory/name/tadashi-tokieda/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Besides his native language Japanese, he is also fluent in French and English. In addition, he knows ancient Greek, Latin, classical Chinese, Finnish, Spanish, and Russian.<ref name="issmys.eu">{{Cite web |title=bio |url=http://www.issmys.eu/previous-year/lyon/instructors-folder/tadashi-tokieda |website="Modern Mathematics" International summer school for students}}</ref> When asked how many languages he knows, he answered "I don't really know. It's like asking how many friends you have."<ref>{{cite news |last=Herzberg |first=Nathaniel |date=9 June 2023 |title=直感の逆を突き、驚かせ、人の未知への欲求を刺激する 仏紙が唸る「数学を世間に広める能力で、時枝正にかなう者はいない」 |trans-title=He goes against intuition, surprises people, and stimulates their desire for the unknown. A French newspaper raves: "No one can match Tokieda Tadashi in his ability to popularize mathematics to the public." |url=https://courrier.jp/news/archives/328428/ |language=Japanese |work=[[Courrier Japon]] |location= |access-date=October 21, 2024 |quote=時枝はいったい何ヵ国語に通じているのだろうか。 「よくわからないんです。言ってみれば、友達が何人いるのかを問われるようなものです。そんな質問は普通しませんよね」 |trans-quote=Just how many languages does Tokieda know? "I don't really know. It's like asking how many friends you have. No one normally asks that question."}}</ref> So far he has lived in eight countries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stony Brook University |date=27 October 2016 |title=Five Questions With Tadashi Tokieda |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YGgIKSXgYAg |via=YouTube}}</ref>

In March 2020, Tokieda was interviewed on ''The Joy of X'', [[Steven Strogatz]]'s podcast for ''[[Quanta Magazine]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 March 2020 |title=Tadashi Tokieda's Special Kind of Magic |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/tadashi-tokiedas-special-kind-of-magic-20200310/ |access-date=11 March 2020 |publisher=Quanta Magazine}}</ref>
